title: Per-model memory profiles for Llama / Mistral / Qwen long-context variants
creator: Liam Chen
description: Objective: Create and integrate model-specific GPU memory profiles for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen family models, with explicit support for long-context configs (8k / 32k). These profiles should allow the serving runtime to make deterministic trade-offs between KV cache residency, batch concurrency, and attention kernel selection to meet latency SLOs while avoiding OOMs on common GPU types (A10G, A100-40GB, H100-80GB).
background: We frequently see SLO violations or OOMs when serving long-context variants (llama-2-70b-32k, mistral-7b-8k, qwen-14b-32k) under continuous batching. Root causes: KV cache size grows with sequence length and token churn, memory fragmentation across CUDA allocations, and suboptimal kernel choices for large seq lengths. Current auto heuristics are conservative and either underutilize hardware or blow up memory in rush periods.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model profile JSONs added to model catalog for the initial set: llama-2-70b-8k, llama-2-70b-32k, mistral-instruct-7b-8k, qwen-14b-32k.
Serving runtime uses profile to pick: kv cache sharding strategy, max concurrent batch size, and kernel variant (triton vs cuBLAS fused) at model load time.
Regression dashboard shows <=10% latency regression for P50 and no increase in OOM rate on nightly stability tests for A10G and A100-40GB compared to baseline.
Canary rollout plan in console with fallback to 'balanced' profile on memory pressure.
Automated unit/integration tests cover edge cases: sudden context length shift, prefix caching warmup, and graceful fallback when fragmentation threshold exceeded.
technical_notes: Profiling results will include: per-layer kv byte footprint, peak activation memory, allocator fragmentation snapshot, and kernel memory overhead. We'll implement a lightweight profile format: {"model": "", "context": "", "kv_bytes_per_token": "", "recommended_batch_max": "", "preferred_kernel": "", "swap_strategy": ""} stored as JSON in model catalog. Runtime will query profile and compute reservation = max(activation_peak, kv_reservation + reserved_slab). For long-context models we will enable KV sharding across device memory vs host pinned memory (with async prefetch) as an opt-in parameter in profile.
profiling_summary: Initial microbenchmarks on A100-40GB (llama-2-70b-32k): kv_bytes_per_token ~ 280 bytes, peak activations ~ 12 GB at max_length=32k with batch=1. With batching=4 naive approach exceeded 40GB. Mistral-7b-8k peak activations ~ 4.2 GB, kv_bytes_per_token ~ 96 bytes. Qwen-14b-32k shows high kernel temp allocations during attention and benefits from Triton fused attention kernels when sequence > 8k. Observed fragmentation when using standard cudaMalloc/free patterns; cudamalloc_async reduces peak by ~5-7% in our harness.
experiment_results: Exp-1: aggressive kv sharding to host pinned memory reduced GPU resident by 60% but added avg 8-12ms per token for tail requests; acceptable for background batch workloads but not P50-sensitive paths.
Exp-2: per-model 'low_gpu' profile that downshifts to int8-quantized attention kernels reduced memory by ~28% for Mistral with negligible quality impact (BLEU-like eval on evalsets).
Exp-3: dynamic batch cap computed from profile + current free memory prevented OOMs in stress test and maintained throughput within 92% of baseline.
Exp-4: enabling cudamalloc_async + memory pooling decreased allocation churn and reduced 95th percentile latency by ~6% in sustained QPS tests.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Using host-sharded KV reduces GPU memory pressure but increases latency and network dependency.
- Aggressive quantization profiles risk output quality regressions; must be gated behind eval thresholds.
- Allocator changes (cudamalloc_async) may interact poorly with custom third-party kernels; need compatibility tests.
- Adding profile selection logic increases runtime complexity and potential for misconfiguration; provide sane fallbacks.
implementation_plan: 1) Add profile schema and catalog entries (week 1). 2) Implement profile-driven reservation in runtime memory manager and kernel selector (week 2-3). 3) Integrate KV sharding code path and host-pinned prefetch (week 3). 4) Add canary rollout + console flagging and dashboarding (week 4). 5) Run extended nightlies and fix regressions (week 5).
progress_updates: 2026-01-12: Bootstrapped profiling harness for Llama/Mistral/Qwen in perf-lab. Saved raw traces to GCS (gs://redwood-perf/ENG-6729/).

2026-01-18: Completed raw memory charters for llama-2-70b-32k and mistral-7b-8k. Added initial 'balanced' profile drafts to model catalog. Pushed draft to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2156

2026-01-26: Ran stress test with continuous batching at 400 RPS against 8k Mistral; observed fragmentation pattern tied to attention kernel temp buffers. Added cudamalloc_async experiment (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2169).
2026-02-04: Code review feedback from Noah Becker: require explicit integration tests and guard rails when host-shard enabled. Added integration test plan to PR.

2026-02-10: Canary rollout started to internal group 'alpha' on A100 pool with profile 'llama-2-70b-32k-balanced'. No OOMs so far. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime/memory-profiles

2026-02-15: Found a regression on Qwen-14b when preferred_kernel set to 'triton-fused' on H100: 2% increase in P50 latency due to kernel scheduling preemption. Reverted for H100 in profile; investigating scheduling knobs.
qa_notes: Create synthetic workload that varies context length mid-request and ensure runtime either gracefully limits batch or swaps KV pages. Nightly stability should run 12-hour continuous batching with context mix: 60% short (512), 30% mid (8k), 10% long (32k). Fail build on OOM > 0 in nightlies.
next_steps: Address H100 scheduling regression: coordinate with infra to test kernel launch affinity and cgroup CPU pinning.
Finalize profile schema and add validation in model catalog CI.
Add regression alerting in console tied to memory-profile rollouts (automated rollback on OOM spike).
Schedule cross-team review with Platform and Performance to validate host-sharding security implications.
